documents.text:
September 24, 2026



Christine Turner, Executive Director
Historical Society of Dauphin County
219 South Front Street
Harrisburg, PA 17104

SUBJECT:       CONCLUSION OF SECTION 106 CONSULTATION AND NOTICE OF
               AVAILABILITY OF THE FINAL ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT FOR
               CONSTELLATION ENERGY GENERATION, LLC’S LICENSING AND
               REGULATORY REQUESTS FOR REAUTHORIZATION OF POWER
               OPERATIONS AT CHRISTOPHER M. CRANE CLEAN ENERGY CENTER
               (EPID NUMBER: L-2025-LNE-0008) (DOCKET NUMBER: 50-289)

Dear Christine Turner:

The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) staff has completed its environmental review
and National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) Section 106 consultation regarding the series of
licensing and regulatory requests submitted by Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (CEG)
that seek NRC approvals to reauthorize power operations at the Christopher M. Crane Clean
Energy Center (CCEC) (formerly Three Mile Island Nuclear Station, Unit 1). The CCEC is
located on Three Mile Island within the Susquehanna River in Londonderry Township, Dauphin
County, Pennsylvania. In accordance with Section 106 of the NHPA and paragraph 800.8(c) of
Title 36 of the Code of Federal Regulations (36 CFR) Part 800–the regulations implementing
NHPA Section 106–the NRC staff used the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, as
amended (NEPA), process to comply with NHPA Section 106 in lieu of the procedures set forth
in 36 CFR 800.3 through 800.6. The NRC served as the lead Federal agency for the
environmental review under NEPA and for NHPA Section 106 consultation, with the U.S.
Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing as a cooperating agency.

In a letter dated February 2, 2026 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management System
(ADAMS) Accession No. ML26023A173), the NRC initiated Section 106 consultation with the
Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission, State Historic Preservation Office (PA
SHPO; Project Number 2026PR00595) and met virtually with PA SHPO staff on March 2, 2026.
The NRC also notified Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) and initiated Section
106 consultation with 15 federally recognized Indian Tribes by letter dated February 2, 2026
(ML26023A133). The Stockbridge-Munsee Community responded by email on February 3,
2026, stating that the undertaking was outside of their traditional homeland and area of interest
and that they had no further comment regarding the project (ML26035A176).

On March 3, 2026, the PA SHPO responded by letter requesting modifications to the area of
potential effects (APE) maps, photographs, and construction dates for the CCEC training facility
and simulator building and recommended including local preservation interests in the
consultation process (ML26062A273). The ACHP also responded by letter on February 11,
2026, noting a potential inconsistency in the APE description and maps transmitted by the NRC
with the Section 106 initiation letter (ML26111A167). One Indian Tribe responded by email
 C. Turner                                     -2-


dated March 25, 2026, requesting a non-public, virtual, Tribal information meeting (as offered by
the NRC in the Section 106 initiation letter).

The NRC staff prepared additional, revised, APE maps and transmitted them to all consulting
parties by letters dated March 31, 2026 (ML26085A035 and ML26085A065). At the same time,
the NRC initiated consultation with four historic preservation organizations (ML26096A404 and
ML26085A688). The Middletown Historical Restoration Commission accepted the NRC’s
invitation to participate in the Section 106 process by email dated April 15, 2026
(ML26111A093). By letters dated April 21, 2026, and April 27, 2026, the PA SHPO
acknowledged receipt of the revised APE maps and project scope and concurred with the
NRC’s delineation of the APE for the undertaking (ML26111A329 and ML26117A202).

In response to the PA SHPO’s request for additional information pertaining to the CCEC training
facility and simulator building, the NRC staff visited the facility on April 8, 2026, to gather
additional construction details and photographs. This supplemental information was transmitted
to the PA SHPO by letter dated April 30, 2026 (ML26119A728). On May 28, 2026, the PA
SHPO concurred that, based on currently available information, the training facility and
simulator building are not eligible for the National Register of Historic Places (ML26149A290).

On May 5, 2026, the NRC facilitated a non-public, virtual, Tribal information meeting. While
representatives from five Indian Tribes accepted the meeting invitation, none were able to
attend (ML26139A188). The NRC distributed the meeting presentation virtually to all 14
federally recognized Indian Tribes on May 14, 2026 (ML26139A187).

On June 4, 2026, the NRC notified all consulting parties (ML26149A199, ML26149A244,
ML26149A291) and transmitted the draft environmental assessment (EA) and draft finding of no
significant impact (FONSI) for review and comment and was issued to PA SHPO for review and
concurrence. The draft EA and draft FONSI were also made available for public review and
comment through publication of a Federal Register notice (see 91 FR 34658).

In the draft EA and draft FONSI letters to Section 106 consulting parties, the NRC staff
explained that in Section 3.9 of the draft EA described the historic and cultural resources and
historic properties identified within the APE, assessed potential impacts on those resources, and
presented preliminary determinations under NHPA and NEPA. The final EA and FONSI, “Final
Environmental Assessment and Finding of No Significant Impact for the Christopher M. Crane
Clean Energy Center Reauthorization of Power Operations Project,” (ML26231A018); available
from the NRC’s CCEC website: https://www.nrc.gov/facilities-safety/facility-finder/reactors/ccec,
include the finalized information and determinations in Section 3.9.

The draft EA and draft FONSI concluded that the undertaking would result in no adverse effect
on historic properties under Section 106 and that impacts to historic and cultural resources
would not be significant under NEPA. By letter dated June 29, 2026 (ML26180A256), the PA
SHPO concurred with the NRC’s Section 106 determination, specifically that the undertaking will
have no adverse effect on the Three Mile Island, Unit 2 National Historic District, and that the
undertaking will have no effect on several nearby archaeological sites. On July 8, 2026, the
Absentee Shawnee Tribe indicated no objections to the proposed project but requested the PA
SHPO report, any future archaeological survey results, and notification of any inadvertent
discoveries of archaeological materials, remains, or cultural items (ML26190A021). On July 24,
2026, the Middletown Historical Restoration Commission stated it had no issues with the project
(ML26208A034). These findings remain unchanged in the final EA and FONSI.
 C. Turner                                    -3-


If you have any questions concerning the NRC’s Section 106 consultation or the environmental
review, please contact Jennifer Davis, Archaeologist, by phone at 301-415-3835 or via email at
Jennifer.Davis@nrc.gov, or the Environmental Project Manager, Kevin Folk, by phone at 301-
415-6944 or via email at Kevin.Folk@nrc.gov.

                                            Sincerely,


                                                           Signed by Steve Koenick on 09/24/26

                                            Stephen S. Koenick, Chief
                                            License Renewal Environmental Branch
                                            Division of Licensing Projects II
                                            Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation
